question: Does the inference-time KG-context relevance study (KGSweetSpot) already cover the training-time relevance-selection modification, leaving only a stage difference, and does that stage difference produce a demonstrably different effect?
description: The most promising modification (M002, relevance-selected context) may be substantially pre-empted: the IKG/KGSweetSpot study already compares triple-based vs. path-based KG knowledge representations, evaluates relevance filtering strategies, and shows that imprecise selection degrades below zero-shot, with public code; ToG-3 and GNN-RAG also perform adaptive/learned context selection. The remaining distinction is stage (training supervision vs. inference prompt) and task (multi-hop KGQA training vs. multiple-choice QA prompting), which has not been verified to matter.
rationale: If relevance filtering of KG context is already thoroughly studied, modification M002 cannot stand as a distinct contribution and the investigation must lean entirely on the matched-budget training-time causal test (M001).
